def: A language model prompted to grade another system's output against a written criterion.
The written definition of a criterion, including what counts as PASS and FAIL, that a judge applies.
A judgement in which a judge sees two answers to the same question and says which is better.
A judge's tendency to prefer the answer shown first or second regardless of content.
A judge's tendency to prefer longer answers even when the extra length adds nothing.
A judge's tendency to prefer answers written by itself or by a model of its own family.
Judging each pair in both orders and counting a win only when the verdict agrees across orders.
Of the outputs humans label PASS, the fraction the judge also passes.
Of the outputs humans label FAIL, the fraction the judge also fails.
An estimate of the true pass rate from a judge's observed rate and its true positive and negative rates.
